title: Jollof Rice
description: Long-grain rice braised down in a blended pepper base until every grain is stained red. The base is fried hard before the rice goes near it — that is the whole difference between jollof and tomato rice.
notes: Parboiled long-grain rice is not a shortcut. It holds its shape through a long covered braise where basmati turns to porridge.

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet
ingredients.note: stem removed; halve the heat by deseeding

steps.text: Blend the red bell peppers, plum tomatoes, scotch bonnet, and half the onion to a smooth purée.
steps.tip: Taste the raw purée before it goes in the pan. That is the only honest read you get on how hot the pot will be.

steps.text: Pour the purée into a wide pan and boil it down hard, uncovered, until it darkens and stops smelling raw.
In a heavy pot, fry the sliced onion in the groundnut oil until golden, then add the tomato paste and cook it until it turns brick red.
Stir the reduced purée into the paste and keep frying until oil pools at the edges of the pot.
steps.tip: Wait for the oil to separate. Rice added to a wet base steams instead of frying, and it never catches up.

steps.text: Rinse the parboiled rice in several changes of water until the water runs clear, then drain it well.
Add the chicken stock, curry powder, dried thyme, bay leaves, and salt to the base and bring it up to a hard boil.
Stir in the rice once, level it, seal the pot with foil under a tight lid, and cook on the lowest heat without lifting it.
steps.tip: The foil is the recipe. Steam that escapes is water the top layer of rice never gets.

steps.text: Dot the butter over the top, fork the grains through from the bottom up, and let the pot stand off the heat before serving.
